Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What failed
  In XMLModelTestCase.testAxisAttribute(), the assertion for the wildcard attribute selection on a namespaced element fails:
  vendor/product/price:amount/@* is expected to return the set {"10%", "20%"} (both a prefixed attribute price:discount="10%" and an unprefixed attribute discount="20%"), but only the unprefixed attribute is returned.

- How the selection is implemented
  For attribute wildcards, DOMAttributeIterator iterates over all attributes and filters them with testAttr(Attr):
  - The iterator’s constructor branches into the wildcard path when name.getName().equals("*") and calls testAttr for each Attr.
  - In testAttr(Attr attr) (lines 68–98):
    - It extracts the attribute’s prefix and local name.
    - It skips xmlns attributes.
    - If the requested local name is "*" (wildcard) or matches the attribute’s local name, it then checks namespace/prefix:
      - It obtains testPrefix = name.getPrefix() from the requested QName (for "@*" this is null).
      - It returns true if equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix).
      - Otherwise, it resolves both prefixes to namespace URIs (if present) and returns true only if those URIs are equal.

- Why the bug occurs
  For the expression "@*", the requested QName has:
  - testLocalName = "*" (wildcard)
  - testPrefix = null (no namespace restriction)
  When encountering a namespaced attribute (e.g., price:discount):
  - nodePrefix = "price"
  - equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix) is false because equalStrings(null, "price") returns false.
  - testNS remains null (since testPrefix is null), while nodeNS resolves to the URI bound to "price" (e.g., "priceNS").
  - equalStrings(testNS, nodeNS) => equalStrings(null, "priceNS") is false.
  Therefore, testAttr returns false and the namespaced attribute is incorrectly excluded from @*.

- Evidence from the bug report
  The current issue report “Namespaced attribute not selected with wildcard” describes exactly this: xml/@* fails to select a namespaced attribute x:pop. The suggested fix matches the observed code:
  - Change the prefix check from:
    if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) { return true; }
  - To:
    if (testPrefix == null || equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) { return true; }
  This change means: when the test expression has no prefix (i.e., no namespace restriction), accept any attribute prefix in wildcard mode, which aligns with XPath semantics that @* selects all attributes regardless of namespace.

- Consequence in the failing test
  In vendor/product/price:amount/@*, the unprefixed attribute discount="20%" is included (nodePrefix null, testNS and nodeNS both null, so equalStrings returns true), but price:discount="10%" is excluded due to the faulty null-prefix handling described above. Hence the test expecting {"10%", "20%"} fails.

Root Cause:
DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr incorrectly treats a null test prefix as a mismatch during wildcard attribute selection, thereby excluding namespaced attributes from @*. The method needs to consider testPrefix == null as “match any prefix” in the wildcard/local-name match case.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
